meta.title: BI & Data Warehouse Audit | Agentic Governance
meta.description: A BI and data warehouse audit traces a management number from source to report — grain, joins, history, reconciliation, ownership — and returns a prioritized findings register you can act on.

title: Can you reproduce this number — and explain where it changes?
intro: When two reports disagree or a warehouse is inherited, the fastest way forward is to follow one real number through the system. We trace a management indicator from its sources, through transformations, to the report — and hand back evidence, exposure, and a prioritized fix list.

triggers.heading: Recognizable situations
items: A BI lead inherits a warehouse and nobody can say which numbers are authoritative.
Two reports present the same KPI with different totals, and Finance is preparing to consolidate reporting.
A platform migration or ERP change is coming and the reporting baseline needs to be trusted first.

method.heading: How a review runs
method.intro: The method is deliberately narrow: one indicator, one reference total, one trace.
steps: Select a management indicator and its reference total (for example, a freight or revenue figure Finance relies on).
Trace it from source systems through transformations — SQL Server queries, ETL steps, semantic models — into the report, e.g. a Power BI dataset.
Inspect grain, join keys, slowly changing history, reconciliation points, and ownership.
Deliver a findings register: what breaks, the evidence, the exposure, and the estimated effort to fix.

fields.label: Decision
fields.text: Can Finance use the report's freight total?

fields.label: Evidence
fields.text: Two orders have freight charges of $12 and $8. The first has three lines, the second has one. After the join to order lines, the report adds $12 three times and $8 once, for $44. The order register totals $20.

fields.label: Finding and action
fields.text: Freight is recorded per order. Aggregate at order level before combining totals, then reconcile to the register. The example passes when the report returns $20 and the detail still shows four lines.

deliverables.heading: What you receive
items: An executive summary written for the budget holder, not the engineering team.
A source-to-report trace of the selected indicator, with the evidence at each hop.
A prioritized findings register: evidence, exposure, and estimated effort per item.
Optional coaching while your team applies selected corrections.

provides.heading: What we need from you
items: Read access to the warehouse and the report in scope (read-only is sufficient).
A named owner who can answer questions about the indicator's definition.
One representative number that currently causes disagreement.

cta.heading: Discuss a project
cta.text: Fixed scope can be quoted once a representative sample, access assumptions, and deliverables are defined. Email to start the conversation.
